key_insight: Boundary-layer detachment and breakdown of Prandtl scaling can coexist with convergence toward a smooth Euler flow as the Reynolds number increases.
engineering_relevance: These results inform high-Reynolds-number CFD validation by showing that local boundary-layer breakdown need not imply failure of global energy-norm convergence.
method: Direct numerical simulations of two-dimensional incompressible flow in a periodic channel with no-slip walls.
Reynolds-dependent initial conditions with Prandtl-thickness boundary layers approaching an analytic, stationary Euler flow.
Track detachment, velocity-difference energy, and time-averaged dissipation as Reynolds number increases.
evidence_signal: Highly resolved simulations show both the squared velocity-difference energy norm and time-averaged energy dissipation scaling approximately as Re^(-1/2) over the simulated interval.
watch_item: The evidence is numerical and limited to the simulated two-dimensional setup and time interval; it does not establish general or long-time convergence.
paper_title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
